newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal up, carloads off from yr ago.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal up, carloads off from yr ago.

text.p: U.S. rail intermodal freight rose in the week ended April 12 from the same week a year ago, while carloads and ton-miles declined due to inclement weather in the upper Midwest, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
AAR said intermodal traffic in the week totaled 167,152 trailers and containers, up 13.4 percent from 147,458 in the year-ago week. Intermodal does not include carloads.

Carloads in week fell 3.3 percent to 332,997 from 344,394 in the same 1996 week, while ton-miles stood at 25.3 billion, off 3.4 percent from 26.2 billion last year. A ton-mile equals one ton of freight hauled one mile.
"The weather particularly affected the western railroads' loadings of coal and grain," Craig Rockey, AAR senior assistant vice president, said in a statement.
"The areas where the weather was worst don't originate much intermodal traffic, however, so intermodal continued to show the strength it has all year," Rockey added.
AAR said that carloads of grain in the April 12 week plunged 18.9 percent to 22,883 from 28,224 in the year-ago week, while coal fell 8.5 percent to 120,783 carloads from 132,055.

Nonmetallic minerals carloads also fell 15.7 percent to 8,298 from 9,848 a year ago, while primary forest products produced 7,008 carloads, down 6.6 percent from 7,506 last year. Grain mill products loadings also fell 2.9 percent to 9,200 carloads from 9,471.

But petroleum products loadings increased 15.8 percent to 6,272 carloads from 5,416 in the year-ago week. Lumber and wood products also rose 7.3 percent to 5,673 carloads from 5,288 last year, while metals and related products climbed 6.9 percent to 12,675 carloads from 11,854.
AAR also said metallic ores loadings rose 1.6 percent to 19,352 from 19,050 a year ago, while chemicals increased 2.6 percent to 32,360 carloads in the week from 31,551 last year.

In the first 15 weeks of 1997, AAR said intermodal traffic rose 5.9 percent from the same period in 1996. Ton-miles rose 3.3 percent while carloads increased 2.7 percent from the same 1996 period, it said.

AAR also said carloads on the two U.S. Canada-based railroads totaled 25,495 trailers and containers, up 11.5 percent from the year-ago week, while carloads totaled 52,020, down seven percent from a year ago.

In the first 15 weeks of 1997, U.S. railroads in Canada hauled 356,834 trailers and containers, a 9.4 percent increase from the same period in 1996, and 769,935 carloads, up 0.1 percent from the year-ago period, AAR said.

Combined total volume in the United States and Canada for the first 15 weeks was 5.80 million carloads, up 2.3 percent from the same 1996 period, while intermodal traffic totaled 2.74 million trailers and containers, up 6.3 percent, it said.
